prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1414; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- The patient was treated for the same body area within the last two years, and that condition adds to the current complaints.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Received first notice of loss for a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. The insured reports being stopped when the other vehicle struck the rear bumper, and the claimant is listed as the passenger in the struck vehicle. Confirmed the insured driver is named on the policy and coverage was in force at the time of loss.

Entry 2: Police report obtained. The reporting officer and two independent witnesses confirm the claimant was seated in the vehicle and that the impact occurred as described. Scene photos and the other driver's statement match the account given at first notice.

Entry 3: Inspected the damaged vehicle. The rear bumper, trunk lid and tail lamp assembly show damage consistent with the reported impact angle and speed. No prior damage to the vehicle is known from the file or from the insured's history with us.

Entry 4: Claimant is represented by counsel, and all contact is now routed through the attorney's office. Counsel submitted a demand package including medical records for neck and upper back complaints. The claimant has since added a few minor details to the account, but the core description of the crash has stayed consistent across statements.

Entry 5: Reviewed the medical records. The claimant was treated for the same neck and upper back area within the past two years, and that prior condition appears to add to the current complaints. At this stage it is not yet clear how much of the present injury, if any, came from this collision.

Entry 6: Treatment followed a typical course of care, with physical therapy and follow-up visits tapering off as the claimant's symptoms improved. Nothing in the records suggests the treatment pattern departs from what would be expected for this type of injury. Requested an independent medical review to help separate the prior condition from the current complaints.

Entry 7: Coverage confirmed in force at the time of loss, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start. Reserves reviewed and held pending the independent medical review and counsel's response to our request for additional records.
